claim.why_it_matters: 15.73.3 rule 3 states the EXACT value FUNCTION PI returns under standard-decimal arithmetic - a hard requirement on the implementation, not an approximation. The PDF prints an unbroken 33-decimal-digit run; the markdown injects a space before the final four digits ('...327 9503'), so a copy that stops at the space yields a value wrong from the 30th decimal onward.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED by pixel measurement of the 300 dpi render, not by eyeballing, and both quotations are accurate. PDF side: on spec_p933.png the rule-3 value occupies the text row band y=1865..1897, x span 556..1407. I profiled every blank-column run inside that span; all 35 inter-glyph gaps measure 4-8 px and NOT ONE reaches 10 px. For same-page calibration of what a genuine word space measures in this font at this size, the two spaces flanking the '+' on the rule-1 line (band y=1391..1432) measure 17 px and 15 px. A real space is therefore ~2.5x the widest gap anywhere in the rule-3 digit run: the PDF categorically prints '3.141592653589793238462643383279503.' unbroken, with no space before '9503'. Markdown side: the space is in the canonical transcription, not just the workunit slice - specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 37356 reads '3.14159265358979323846264338327 9503.'. Every standard rejection route was tested and fails: the text is not reflowed or continued on an adjacent line (the markdown value sits complete on one unwrapped line with an interior space); it is not page-break furniture, wrapping, or hyphenation; neither source is misquoted. The 'does not change meaning' route is the only arguable one and it also fails, because inside a numeric literal whitespace is not formatting - it splits one token into two, and the break falls after the 29th fractional digit, matching no digit-grouping convention (ISO's actual grouping convention on this very page is the comma, per rule 2's '16,312,081,666,...'). Independent check that the PDF reading is the correct one: pi = 3.14159265358979323846264338327950288..., whose 34th fractional digit is 8, so pi correctly rounded to 33 places is ...79503, matching the printed glyphs exactly.
verdict.corrected_description: Real, but the claim is under-scoped and its statement of harm is loose. SCOPE: the identical artifact occurs TWICE on this page. Rule 1 has the same defect - specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 37348 reads '(3 + 0.14159265358979323846264338327 95)' where the PDF prints the unbroken '(3 + 0.1415926535897932384626433832795)' (31-digit run, inter-glyph gaps 3-7 px against the 15-17 px real spaces on the same line). Both breaks land after the 29th fractional digit, so this is one systematic extraction artifact, not two typos, and the fix must repair both lines. HARM: 'yields a value wrong from the 30th decimal onward' must not be read as the transcription carrying wrong digits. All 33 fractional digits are present, correctly ordered, and identical to the PDF; delete the one space and the strings match character for character. The exposure is confined to a mechanical consumer that tokenizes on whitespace - truncating rule 3 at the space yields 3.14159265358979323846264338327 (29 fractional digits, silently dropping '9503'), and truncating rule 1 likewise drops the trailing '95'. A human reader loses nothing, so 'cosmetic' is defensible; the only argument for grading it minor rather than cosmetic is that the affected text is a value-bearing exact-conformance constant (15.73.3 rule 3 fixes an EXACT required return value) rendered as an unparseable two-token string. FIX: delete the single space at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:37348 and :37356.
